transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I guess what finally made me come in is how tense I feel physically. My neck, shoulders, and jaw are tight almost all the time now—like I’m bracing for bad news, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to watch TV at night.
Did this start after something very stressful or upsetting happened in your life?
Yeah, I think it really started after the pipe burst at our house. The remodeling afterward threw everything into chaos, and it’s been going on for about seven months now.
Do you notice the tension gets worse when you think about the pipe burst or the remodeling?

Yeah, I think so. When I start thinking about the house stuff, I notice my jaw tightens and my shoulders sort of creep up. But honestly, it’s not only then—it happens even when I’m just at my desk or sitting watching TV, like my body is bracing for something.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just the house remodeling?

Yes. It’s not just the remodeling. My mind jumps around a lot—like, I’ll worry the contractors missed something, then suddenly I’m thinking my lesson plans aren’t good enough, or the robotics students are falling behind. And then I start worrying I’m letting my wife and family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.
When you start worrying, is it hard to stop or control the worrying?

Yes, it is. I’ll tell myself, okay, stop thinking about this and focus on the class in front of me. But then one little thing, like a late invoice or a student falling behind, sets off this whole chain of what-ifs, and I can’t seem to shut it down.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes. I feel pretty wound up most of the day, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong. At school I catch myself pacing around the classroom, and between periods I’ll keep checking my phone to see if the contractor messaged me.
Do you get tired easily?

Yes. By the time the last bell rings, I feel really wrung out. It’s not the kind of tired that a decent night’s sleep or a quiet Sunday really fixes. Even grading a small stack of quizzes can feel like I’m pushing through mud.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I have moments where my mind drifts, but I haven’t noticed a major problem with concentrating specifically. It’s hard to say.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s a clear problem. Some nights are better than others, but I haven’t really been tracking it or noticed a definite pattern.
Have you been more irritable than usual lately?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself snapping more than usual, or at least no one’s pointed it out to me. I can get frustrated sometimes, but I don’t know that it’s more than normal.
If the house remodeling were completely resolved, do you think most of this tension and worrying would go away?

I think some of it would ease up, sure, but no, I don’t think it would all go away. My mind doesn’t just stay on the remodeling. It jumps from whether the contractors missed something, to whether my lesson plans are slipping, to whether the robotics kids are falling behind… and then I start worrying I’m letting my wife or family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.
